clue.text: Cosmetic exercise for all to see in Pope's action?

indicators.note: one thing set in another means it goes inside it, so the first piece is placed within the second

parts.note: the Pope declares a dead person blessed, the step before sainthood
U is the British film certificate for a film suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A makeover staged publicly, as if the Pope himself were doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: BEATIFICATION and BEAUTIFICATION differ by a single U: drop the universal film rating into the Pope's act. A U certificate marks a British film as fit for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something prettier is a cosmetic undertaking, so the improving process matches that phrase.

clue.text: Like some of the accountant's figures presented for discussion

definitions.text: Like some of the accountant's figures
definitions.meaning: first meaning: balances carried over from a previous page or period
second meaning: put forward, proposed, raised at a meeting

explanation.walkthrough: In bookkeeping a total carried from the bottom of one page to the top of the next bears this label.
explanation.definitionFit: Ledger totals carried over are labelled this way, and a proposal raised at a meeting is likewise said to be put up so.

clue.text: Vulgar American four entertained by their President no longer

indicators.note: a host entertains guests within the home, so the earlier pieces sit inside the later one

parts.note: Abe Lincoln, the Americans' president of long ago
US is the standard abbreviation for American
four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A crude American foursome are hosted by a former president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their' refers back to American: Honest Abe Lincoln was a US president, now long gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive language is coarse and insulting, so vulgar serves as a loose synonym for it.

clue.text: One not expected to score is emotional about excellent half-century

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word wraps around the others

parts.note: tender feelings are emotional ones
A1, first class, written with I for the one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A cricketer welling up after a fine fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a tail-ender is one of the last, weakest batsmen; a half-century is fifty runs, which such a player rarely makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's lower-order batsmen bat last because they are poor at batting, so nobody expects runs from them.

clue.text: Lard that is besetting bloke mostly responsible for enervation

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: lard is pig fat
i.e., Latin id est

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a guy is a bloke

explanation.surface: Fatty food blamed for a man's lack of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Enervation is weakness and loss of vitality, essentially the same as tiredness or exhaustion.

clue.text: Clown, eccentric — one of a lovely bunch?

parts.note: Coco was a famous circus clown
a nut is a crazy or eccentric person

explanation.surface: A daft clown sounds like a lovely bunch of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes the music-hall song 'I've Got a Lovely Bunch of Coconuts'; the question mark flags the indirect reference.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known comic song celebrates a lovely bunch of these tropical fruits hanging up at a fairground shy.

clue.text: Trunk coming from gnarled roots

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted and knotted, so these letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree trunk growing out of twisted roots.
explanation.walkthrough: Trunk and roots paint a tree, but the trunk wanted is the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human body, without head or limbs, is called by this Italian-derived word.

clue.text: Late deliveries on the field — water on the ground, we hear?

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its spoken sound, not its spelling

parts.note: dew is moisture settled on grass

explanation.surface: Cricket running late, with dew on the outfield.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six deliveries from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has passed the time it was expected, so it is late.

clue.text: Various pieces in street I coveted, but he may have deterred me!

indicators.note: breaking the words into various pieces lets their letters be rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A would-be shoplifter eyes goods in a shop street but is put off by a watcher.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the shoplifter's confession: 'I coveted' the pieces, but someone watching stopped me.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain-clothes security officer in a shop exists to deter thieves like the speaker.

clue.text: One can tell when a pupil isn't working

definitions.text: One can tell when a pupil isn't working

parts.words: One can tell when a pupil isn't working
parts.note: surface reading: a schoolteacher spotting a lazy student
setter's reading: the pupil of the eye, which an eye specialist examines

explanation.walkthrough: The pupil is in the eye, not the classroom; 'isn't working' means faulty vision rather than idleness.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye doctor examines vision and can diagnose when part of the eye fails to function properly.

clue.text: Putting money on a dog is commonly practised

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
rent is money paid; it is put on, after, the dog

explanation.surface: Betting on greyhounds is a widespread habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting money on a dog' reads as gambling; in an across answer 'on' places the money after the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Current practice is what is generally done nowadays, in widespread use at present.

clue.text: Someone in uniform teased within earshot

indicators.note: within earshot means as heard by a listener, so the word counts by its sound

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them

explanation.surface: A uniformed person mocked where others can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: A Guide is a member of the Girl Guides, the British equivalent of the Girl Scouts, who wear uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Girl Guides movement wear a uniform, so one fits this description.

clue.text: Beginning to go below, prisoner brought in explosive

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of go

indicators.note: brought in means taken inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: below means under
prisoner of war

explanation.surface: A prisoner tunnelling below ground smuggles in explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunpowder is the original black powder explosive used in firearms and fireworks.

clue.text: Most in street upset about awful din

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one jumble wraps the other
something upset is knocked over and disordered, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: awful suggests a mess, so these letters are jumbled too

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A street in disarray around a terrible racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most in' is the definition: in means fashionable, so most in is most fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: In as slang for fashionable makes the superlative most in equivalent to the most stylish or modish.

clue.text: Beg President to take precedence

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for president
to lead is to go first, taking precedence

explanation.surface: Asking the President to go first.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to ask earnestly or entreat, which is what begging also means.

clue.text: Case getting left with female bits and pieces

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
F is the abbreviation for female
an olio is a miscellany or hotchpotch

explanation.surface: A suitcase abandoned, holding a woman's odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: OLIO, a mixture or medley, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat carrying case for papers or drawings, so case is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Very big vehicle may be what film actor is after

parts.note: OS means outsize, a clothing label for very large
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A huge vehicle might be what a movie star chases after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle' also suggests a film showcasing a star, a deliberate echo.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood actors covet the Academy Award statuette, the industry's top prize for performers.

clue.text: Upright character in church opposing drink

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the others

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
anti means against
the letter I is a single upright stroke

explanation.surface: A moral person in church who disapproves of alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright character' sounds like a virtuous person but means the letter that stands straight up.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, so it is a specific example of an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Twenty years ago Labour MPs were downtrodden!

definitions.text: Twenty years ago Labour MPs were
definitions.meaning: first meaning: led by Michael Foot, Labour leader in the early 1980s

explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983, about twenty years before this puzzle appeared, so its MPs were under Foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lying beneath one's feet is trodden upon, which is the literal sense of downtrodden.

clue.text: Left after dinner?

parts.note: surface reading: departed once the meal was over
setter's reading: remaining on the plate, never consumed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb of going away; it is an adjective for food still there.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that remains on the plate after a meal has not been consumed by anyone.

clue.text: Something in computer — a bit sticking up, almost broken

indicators.note: in a down answer sticking up means the words read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a tad is a little bit

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter goes

parts.note: bust means broken

explanation.surface: A computer part with a piece poking out, nearly broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A data bus is the set of wires inside a computer carrying information between components.

clue.text: Old sailor performing on a soapbox?

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a rating is an ordinary sailor, not an officer

explanation.surface: An old seaman holding forth in public.
explanation.walkthrough: Standing on a soapbox is the traditional image of a street speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Speakers on soapboxes make speeches to passers-by, delivering formal public addresses.

clue.text: Sort of food thing covered in grain

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped by, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: wheat is a grain
an item is a thing

explanation.surface: Some foodstuff coated in cereal, like breaded chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Poultry breast and similar pale flesh is a category of meat, hence a kind of food.

clue.text: Type size for characters used in the literature

indicators.note: the letters needed are among those used in the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the and start of literature

explanation.surface: Choosing a typeface for printing literature.
explanation.walkthrough: Elite was a small typewriter type size, twelve characters to the inch, alongside pica.
explanation.definitionFit: On typewriters the smaller standard typeface, twelve characters per inch, was known by this name.

clue.text: Bread no longer available across the Channel

definitions.text: Bread no longer available across the Channel

parts.words: Bread no longer available across the Channel
parts.note: surface reading: a baguette that French bakers no longer sell
setter's reading: bread as slang for money, a currency the French gave up for the euro

explanation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money; France replaced its old currency with the euro in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: The French former unit of currency was withdrawn when the euro arrived, so this money is gone.

clue.text: Went berserk in diatribe about Brazilian city

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a rant is a tirade
Rio de Janeiro

explanation.surface: Someone lost it in a tirade about Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: Running riot is an idiom for behaving wildly and without restraint, like someone gone mad.

clue.text: Composer of operas using percussion instrument in one

parts.note: a bell is struck to sound
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An opera composer scoring a single percussion instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is not a container signal here; it is kept as a word in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincenzo Bellini was the Italian bel canto composer of Norma and La Sonnambula.

clue.text: To be unseeing, to somehow keep necessarily quiet

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged in some other order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Hamlet-like musing on choosing to stay blind and silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening echoes 'To be or not to be', but those first words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop oneself from speaking, holding back a remark one would like to make.
